articles.title: Preoperative subacromial autologous conditioned plasma (ACP) injections and histological and immunohistochemical findings in degenerative supraspinatus tendon tears - results of a prospective comparative cohort study.
articles.authors: Werner AW, Linke C, Krenn V, Linke P
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroscopic repair of isolated degenerative full-thickness supraspinatus tendon tears
articles.sample_size: 54 patients (24 in ACP group, 30 in control group)
articles.outcomes: Bonar scores, degeneration scores, and immunohistochemical markers (Ki-67, CD31, CD45/LCA) in tendon biopsies taken during surgery
articles.take_home: Patients who received three injections of autologous conditioned plasma before rotator cuff surgery had slightly lower degeneration scores in their tendon samples compared to those who did not receive injections. However, the researchers noted that the differences were small and may not be clinically important.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of a Customized 3D-printed Arthrodesis Prosthesis for Reconstruction of Segmental Defects following Tumor Resection in the Proximal Humerus.
articles.authors: Zhu XJ, Lin JM, Song GH, Lu JC, Xu HY, Zhang T, et al.
articles.population: Patients with malignant tumors of the proximal humerus treated with Malawer type I resection and customized 3D-printed arthrodesis prosthesis reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 30 patients, mean age 20.1 years, mean follow-up 37.7 months
articles.outcomes: MSTS score 84%, ASES score 85%, shoulder abduction 81 degrees, forward flexion 82 degrees, 100% radiographic fusion at 12 months, 7 surgical complications (4 delayed wound healing, 1 prosthetic loosening, 2 plate exposure), 6 soft-tissue failures (20%), no local recurrence
articles.take_home: A customised 3D-printed prosthesis for shoulder reconstruction after tumour removal achieved good functional outcomes with high fusion rates, though total removal of the shoulder muscle (deltoid) increased the risk of complications. This approach appears promising for improving upper limb function in this group of patients.

articles.title: Evolution of Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty: Two Decades of Evidence from the Journal of Shoulder and Elbow Surgery.
articles.authors: Parmar T, Ashkar I, Deshpande V, Parmar N, Daher M, Kane L, et al.
articles.study_type: Bibliometric and content-trend analysis of published research
articles.population: 506 clinical studies on reverse shoulder arthroplasty published in JSES from 2004-2025
articles.outcomes: Publication volume, level of evidence, authorship patterns, research focus, patient demographics, surgical indications, implant design trends, and complication reporting over time
articles.take_home: Research on reverse shoulder arthroplasty in this journal has grown significantly and improved in quality over two decades, with the focus shifting from studying complications towards examining patient outcomes and newer implant designs. The surgery is now used more commonly for osteoarthritis rather than just as a salvage procedure, and implant designs have evolved away from the original Grammont configuration.

articles.title: The medial collapse sign is associated with cubitus varus after pediatric supracondylar humeral fracture fixation: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Ikeda S, Okada S, Shiode R
articles.population: Children treated surgically for supracondylar humeral fractures
articles.outcomes: Association between medial collapse sign on postoperative X-rays and cubitus varus deformity at follow-up
articles.take_home: A radiographic sign called the medial collapse sign was found in 90% of children who developed cubitus varus (a bend in the elbow) after surgery, and was absent in 97% of those who did not develop it. This sign might help surgeons identify during surgery when the fracture alignment needs adjustment to prevent this complication.

articles.title: Comparison of Shoulder Field Anesthesia (SFA) with Interscalene Block (ISB) for Analgesia After Arthroscopic Shoulder Surgery: A Randomized Noninferiority Trial.
articles.authors: Qawasmi F, Gazit T, Mahamid A, Khatib M, Safadi H, Robinson D, et al.
articles.outcomes: Cumulative 48-hour postoperative pain scores using numeric rating scale, patient satisfaction, opioid consumption, hospital stay, and block-related complications
articles.take_home: Shoulder field anesthesia provided pain relief comparable to interscalene block over 48 hours, though interscalene block worked better in the first 4 to 8 hours. Shoulder field anesthesia had fewer serious complications including no cases of Horner syndrome or respiratory problems, shorter hospital stays, and similar patient satisfaction.

articles.title: Predictive Modeling of Clinically Apparent Shoulder Periprosthetic Joint Infection (PJI).
articles.authors: Hsu JE, Ricchetti ET, Tashjian R, Namdari S, Collins AP, Fedorka C, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective multicenter cohort study with predictive modelling
articles.sample_size: 861 consecutive cases; 97 (11%) with shoulder periprosthetic joint infection
articles.outcomes: Development of a seven-factor nomogram to predict clinically apparent shoulder periprosthetic joint infection defined by sinus tract or intra-articular purulence; concordance statistic 0.90
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a predictive model using seven clinical, laboratory, imaging and operative findings that accurately identifies shoulder infections after revision surgery with 90% accuracy in the development cohort. The model requires external validation before it can guide clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Isolated avulsion of the short head of the biceps tendon from the coracoid insertion: A case report and narrative review of the literature.
articles.authors: Damiani L, Consigliere P, West S
articles.outcomes: Return to normal daily and sports activities at 6 months, no anatomical deformity, no clinically evident strength deficit
articles.take_home: This is the first reported case of an isolated short head of biceps tendon tear at its attachment point on the coracoid bone. Surgical repair allowed the patient to return to normal activities without lasting problems.
